methods.label: Use the second and third binomial terms
methods.explanation:
The condition involves only two terms, so we extract them without expanding the whole expression. In descending powers of \(a\), the binomial theorem gives the second term
\[
T_2=na^{n-1}(-b)=-na^{n-1}b
\]
and the third term
\[
T_3=\frac{n(n-1)}2a^{n-2}(-b)^2
=\frac{n(n-1)}2a^{n-2}b^2.
\]
The coefficients have opposite signs because \((-b)^1=-b\) and \((-b)^2=b^2\).

Factoring their sum reveals when they cancel:
\[
T_2+T_3
=na^{n-2}b\left(-a+\frac{n-1}{2}b\right)=0.
\]
Since \(n\ge2\) and \(a,b\ne0\), the factor \(na^{n-2}b\) is nonzero. This includes \(n=2\), when \(a^{n-2}=a^0=1\). Dividing by this factor gives
\[
a=\frac{n-1}{2}b.
\]
Substitute \(a=kb\) and divide by \(b\ne0\):
\[
k=\frac{n-1}{2},
\qquad n=2k+1.
\]
Conversely, this value makes the bracket equal to \(-kb+kb=0\). Every positive integer \(k\) gives an integer \(n\ge3\), so the value satisfies the conditions. Therefore \(\boxed{n=2k+1}\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
